name: hyden

normalize.source: upstream example_code/hyden_load_and_inference.py: transforms.Resize((518,518)) then ToTensor then Normalize with the ImageNet statistics

encoder.source: facebookresearch/metadepth README, checked 2026-08-14: the DA2 variant ships one checkpoint, HyDen-DA2-Large (facebook/hyden-da2-relative-depth). The other two releases are MoGeV2 heads, not smaller DA2 encoders. This repository's rule is to use the smallest released encoder; here that is also the only one

preprocess.verified: adapter exists (evaluate_gt _pil_imagenet_stretch); not yet matched -- reports/inputs/hyden.npy needs the export to run

caveats: hybrid CNN+ViT encoder. It does not replace Depth Anything's DPT head -- it adds CNN feature fusion to it (da2/dpt.py: combine_feats concatenates CNN and ViT features per stage), and HyDenDepthAnything is a wrapper that configures DepthAnything with add_cnn_encoder. Still the first graph here that makes TensorRT fuse convolutions and attention in one engine

upstream preprocesses with torchvision transforms.Resize((518,518)) on a PIL image -- bilinear WITH antialias. depth_anything_v2 uses cv2 INTER_LINEAR, which has none. **Measured on data/example.jpg: the two tensors differ by up to 2.52**, on a tensor whose whole range is -2.12 to 2.64. Not a rounding detail -- downscaling 3024x2268 to 518 aliases the gravel texture hard without antialiasing. This is why the DAv2 adapter is not reused and hyden sits in core.preprocess.UNSUPPORTED

output_form is inverse_depth on upstream's own statement: da2/dpt.py keeps the final activation at ReLU 'to match production DepthAnything decoder behavior (always non-negative inverse depth)'. Larger means nearer. This is read from the source, not measured here -- core.gt.orientation still has to confirm it on DIODE before the row is published, the way zipdepth's -0.892 was

FAIR Noncommercial Research License covers the code AND the weights. It permits derivative works and redistribution provided the agreement travels with them, so it restricts use rather than propagating to this repository's MIT licence -- unlike AGPL, which is why YOLO26-depth was rejected

upstream claims 'up to 10x faster 4K inference' with no GPU named and no numbers published. This repository measures at 518x518 on a pinned-clock RTX 3080; that claim is neither confirmed nor tested by the row it produces
